rows.label: Concept
rows.text: In a crystal, overlapping atomic orbitals split each atomic level into a near-continuous **band**; the highest filled one is the **valence band**, the next the **conduction band**, separated by the **forbidden gap** E_g. **Metals** (Cu, Ag) have overlapping or partly-filled bands — free conduction. **Insulators** (diamond, E_g ≈ 6 eV) have a wide gap (> 3 eV) blocking excitation.…

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: **Bands come from overlap, not from magic** — N atoms split each level into N states.  ·  **E_g > 3 eV = insulator; ~1 eV = semiconductor; 0 = metal.**

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: **Conduction needs electrons in partly-empty bands** — a full band carries no net current.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Valence band, conduction band, forbidden gap E_g; metals overlap, insulators E_g > 3 eV, semiconductors ~1 eV.

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Heating helps semiconductors and hurts metals — opposite signs, same lattice.

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — From Levels to Bands An isolated atom has sharp energy levels. Bring 10²³ atoms together and each level splits into a near-continuous **band**. Which bands are full, empty or partly filled decides whether a solid conducts, insulates or sits in between — the whole story of electronics.  ·  ## 2. Fundamental Concepts (NEB 2023, 2024) ### 2.1 How bands form In a crystal, neighbouring atoms' overlapping wavefunctions make each discrete atomic level split into N closely spaced levels — a **band**. Between bands lie **forbidden gaps** (no allowed states). - **Valence band:** the highest band filled by valence electrons at 0 K.…  ·  ## 3. Conceptual Relationships - **To Topic 113:** the gap size classifies metals, insulators and semiconductors. - **To Topic 114:** doping and intrinsic excitation both populate the conduction band. - **To drift velocity (Topic 98):** carriers in bands drift under fields just as free electrons do.
